verdict.headline: Oil retreats from trigger levels but yields and hike odds reprice ahead of CPI Wednesday
verdict.label: Oil easing pre-CPI; 10Y +8bps to 4.73%, September hike odds ~50%; 30Y still above 5.00%; CRWV AH tonight is the AI demand proxy before Wednesday's 8:30 AM print
verdict.rationale_short: WTI pulled back to ~$78 (below the $79 trigger) and Brent to ~$83.48 (below $85) overnight — positioning-driven, not a Hormuz resolution. Iran's Zolghadr five-condition demand stands, Houthis escalated attacks on Mocha, and Trump is counter-demanding compensation. The bond market is not treating the oil retreat as regime-clearing: 10Y rose 8bps to 4.73% and September hike odds reached ~50%, up 10 percentage points from Monday, while gold hit its highest level since June 5 ($4,432) on safe-haven demand. July CPI arrives Wednesday at 8:30 AM ET; consensus at 3.4% YoY falls in the ambiguous band and leaves Jackson Hole (Aug 27) to decide the rate path. CRWV reports Q2 tonight AH (5 PM ET); DDOG's 17% post-earnings collapse on an AI customer usage cut establishes how the market reads concentration risk into CRWV's MSFT exposure. If SPX closes below 7,600 on or within two sessions of Wednesday's print, the record-proximity bid has broken.

trade_setups.asset: CRWV — Q2 earnings AH tonight, 5 PM ET
trade_setups.thesis: CRWV enters Q2 at ~$90.67 with options pricing a ~12% swing. The AI compute-demand proxy: Q1 contracted backlog was $99.4B with >18-month average duration — the market's confidence level in AI infrastructure monetization. DDOG fell 17% on a beat-and-raise when an AI customer cut usage; CRWV faces the same lens on MSFT concentration. A backlog above $100B and MSFT below 55% reprices Blackwell demand ahead of NVDA's August 26 print. A backlog below $95B or MSFT above 60% reaches NVDA $216 and SPCX $128 in pre-market Wednesday — 14 hours before CPI.
trade_setups.entry: Post-close reaction. NVDA $216 and SPCX $128 are the sympathy levels to watch in Wednesday pre-market for the direction of the read-through.
trade_setups.invalidation: Backlog above $100B, MSFT concentration below 55%, and stable or improving gross margin — NVDA resistance shifts to $221 and the focus fully moves to CPI.
trade_setups.horizon: AH tonight; secondary read Wednesday pre-market.

trade_setups.asset: Oil triggers — will the retreat hold through today's close?
trade_setups.thesis: WTI at ~$78 and Brent at ~$83.48 are below their triggers ($79/$85) for the first time since Saturday, potentially reducing the active regime count from 3-of-6 to 1-of-6 (just the 30Y breach). The retreat is not geopolitically motivated — Zolghadr's conditions stand, Houthis escalated, Trump counter-demanded. It is positioning ahead of CPI. A close above $79 WTI or $85 Brent today re-activates both triggers before Wednesday's print. A close below signals markets are treating the supply-shock premium as priced.
trade_setups.entry: Current: WTI ~$78, Brent ~$83.48. Trigger thresholds: $79 and $85. Watch close prices, not intraday.
trade_setups.invalidation: Any Iran diplomatic escalation or Houthi action that reprices the Hormuz supply-disruption probability pushes WTI back above $79.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's close; CPI Wednesday as the secondary driver of oil direction.

trade_setups.asset: September hike odds — 50% and approaching the formal 70% threshold
trade_setups.thesis: CME FedWatch moved from 40% (Monday close) to ~50% Tuesday morning. The formal regime trigger is 70%. A hot CPI (above 3.2%/3.5%) covers most of the 20-point gap in a session. An in-line print (3.4%/2.5%) holds the market at 45–55% and makes Jackson Hole (Aug 27) the resolution point. A soft print (below 2.9%/3.2%) pushes odds below 30% and removes rate hike as a near-term narrative. Fed speakers today (any Kashkari or Warsh statement on the supply-shock channel) can move odds independently of CPI.
trade_setups.entry: Current: ~50%. Formal threshold: 70%. Watch for any Fed speaker statement today; CPI Wednesday 8:30 AM ET is the primary catalyst.
trade_setups.invalidation: Soft CPI (below 2.9%/3.2%) resets September odds to 25% and removes the 70% formal trigger as a near-term risk.

bear_case: The oil retreat is a pre-CPI position trim in a market still priced for dual resolution — soft CPI and Hormuz deal — neither of which is in hand. Iran's Zolghadr conditions require a post-war settlement; Houthis escalated overnight; Trump's counter-demand makes the diplomatic path longer. The 10Y at 4.73% and September hike odds at 50% are moving in the opposite direction of what the oil retreat implies, suggesting the rate market is front-running the CPI event, not celebrating the oil move. CRWV's backlog and MSFT concentration risk arrive 14 hours before CPI; DDOG established that a beat-and-raise is insufficient when concentration risk reads through. If CRWV misses and CPI is hot, NVDA $216 and SPCX $128 are simultaneously in play. If SPX closes below 7,600 within two sessions of Wednesday's print, the record-proximity bid that has held for five sessions breaks.
